Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

A fair number cube is rolled. What is the theoretical probability of rolling a 3?

feedback.text: Correct. One of the six equally likely outcomes is a 3.
This counts too many favorable outcomes. Only one side is 3.
This is the complement of rolling a 3.
This reverses the probability ratio and is greater than 1.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

A coin is flipped 30 times and lands tails 16 times. What is the experimental probability of tails?

feedback.text: This is the theoretical probability for a fair coin, not the observed data.
Correct. Experimental probability uses observed tails over total flips.
This is the complement count for heads, not tails.
This reverses the ratio. Use favorable observed outcomes over total trials.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

In a survey of 80 people, 20 chose option A. What is the relative frequency for option A?

feedback.text: This is the count that did not choose option A.
This compares option A to not option A, but relative frequency uses the total.
Correct. Relative frequency is the category count divided by the total.
This reverses the ratio and does not represent a probability.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

Which probability is based on observed results?

answer.text: Theoretical probability

feedback.text: Theoretical probability is based on expected outcomes.

answer.text: Equally likely probability

feedback.text: This describes a model, not observed data.

answer.text: Sample space probability

feedback.text: A sample space lists outcomes; it is not necessarily observed data.

answer.text: Experimental probability

feedback.text: Correct. Experimental probability is based on collected or observed results.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

A spinner has 4 equal sections. What is the theoretical probability of landing on one chosen section?

feedback.text: Correct. One favorable section out of four equal sections gives 1/4.
This reverses the probability ratio.
This is the complement of one chosen section.
This would represent two favorable sections, not one.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

In 25 trials, an event happened 10 times. What is the experimental probability?

feedback.text: This is the complement count, not the event count.
Correct. Use observed successes over total trials.
This reverses the ratio.
This compares successes to failures instead of total trials.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

Which statement best compares theoretical and experimental probability?

answer.text: Theoretical uses expected outcomes; experimental uses observed data.

feedback.text: Correct. Theoretical probability comes from a model, while experimental probability comes from results.

answer.text: Theoretical uses observed data; experimental uses expected outcomes.

feedback.text: This reverses the meanings.

answer.text: Both always have to be exactly the same.

feedback.text: They can be different, especially with small samples.

answer.text: Experimental probability cannot be written as a fraction.

feedback.text: Experimental probability is often written as part over total.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

A theoretical probability is most appropriate when:

answer.text: outcomes are equally likely and the probability comes from the model.

feedback.text: Correct. Theoretical probability is based on the structure of the situation.

answer.text: only survey results are given.

feedback.text: Survey results lead to experimental or empirical probability.

answer.text: the sample total is missing.

feedback.text: A probability cannot be found reliably without needed totals.

answer.text: the observed results are different every time.

feedback.text: Changing observed results describe experiments, not the theoretical model.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

In 60 trials, an event did not happen 18 times. What is the experimental probability that it did happen?

feedback.text: This is the probability that it did not happen.
Correct. If it did not happen 18 times, it happened 60 - 18 = 42 times.
This reverses the ratio.
This compares failures to successes, not successes to total trials.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

In a survey of 40 students, 25 prefer videos. What relative frequency represents students who do not prefer videos?

feedback.text: This represents students who prefer videos.
This reverses the needed ratio.
Correct. If 25 prefer videos, then 15 do not, out of 40 total.
This compares the two groups but not to the total.

Question ID: MCR_U05_L02_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.3

Why might experimental probability differ from theoretical probability?

answer.text: Experimental probability never uses data

feedback.text: Experimental probability is based on data.

answer.text: Theoretical probability changes after every trial

feedback.text: The theoretical model does not change because of one trial.

answer.text: Relative frequency cannot be calculated

feedback.text: Relative frequency can be calculated from data.

answer.text: Observed results may vary from the expected model

feedback.text: Correct. Actual data can differ from expected probability, especially with fewer trials.
